messages:
Maya: FYI customer `beta-analytics` reported sudden tail latency regressions after we promoted `int8_balanced_v1` profile to eu-central yesterday evening. p95 jumped ~2.8x, p99 ~3.6x. They're seeing timeouts and some 502s. Opening thread to track triage/mitigation. :rotating_light:

Rishi: can you share the rollout id + which pool (shared/dedicated) and whether it's only for that customer or broad?

Maya: rollout `quant-rollout/2026-03-15-01:18` on eu-central shared pool, targeted to 15% traffic but looks like the customer's traffic got routed to canary instances. Profile excerpt attached below.

Maya: profile (copied):```json
{"name":"int8_balanced_v1","quant":"int8","batch_threshold":16,"kv_prefetch":true,"calibration_mode":"fast"}
```

Tomas: quick thought: `calibration_mode: fast` can under-sample corner cases and cause suboptimal scaling behavior for attention/k-v layout which could provoke kernel fallbacks. Also `kv_prefetch` may increase per-request working set if we pre-touch memory that doesn't fit in cache; combined with mixed kernels that don't have full int8 support, this can increase tail latency.

Rishi: reproduce plan: 1) run short chat traffic (tokens ~30) at bursts of 300 concurrent reqs for 10s windows to simulate their load pattern, 2) use the exact profile on a lab replica with same model binary, 3) collect `kernel_fallback_count`, `gpu_mem_used`, and `op_latency_histogram` for the window. Maya, can you run that?

Maya: running now against a eu-central test replica. curl script using `rb run-load --concurrency 300 --pattern burst --tokens 30 --profile int8_balanced_v1`. Will paste results in 10m.

(10m) Maya: repro confirmed: p95 210ms -> 590ms, p99 1.1s -> 3.9s under canary profile. Observed `kernel_fallback_count` spike per-request (some requests 4-6 fallbacks). GPU mem shows occasional peaks and page faults in the driver logs.

Zara: interesting: int8 normally reduces memory which should help; the fallbacks indicate some ops are forcing conversion to fp16 or CPU paths mid-execution. Need to check whether our conv/attention int8 kernels are enabled for this model variant. Tomas, can you correlate op types hitting fallback?

Tomas: I pulled the traces. Fallbacks concentrated on rotary/rope ops + certain fused attention kernels when seq_len > 128. The calibration step in `fast` mode produced scaling factors that create uncommon sparsity patterns and some ops miss the optimized int8 codegen path. I also see a handful of `tensor-core` selector logs choosing slower kernels when mixed-precision compatibility fails.

Rishi: mitigation checklist: immediate and medium-term. Immediate: 1) pause the canary rollout in eu-central and rollback routes for impacted customers to `fp16-stable` pool (we can do a per-customer override); 2) temporarily disable `kv_prefetch` in the profile; 3) increase tracing to capture 50 failing request traces for infra. Medium: refine quant profile and run extended seq tests before rollout. Maya please execute 1 and 2 now.

Maya: paused rollout @ 01:45UTC. Forced `beta-analytics` to `fp16-stable` via per-customer routing override. Created debug traces and set retention to 72h for those traces.

SupportBot: Incident INC-2026-0315-19 created and linked to ticket #8610. Account team notified.

Tomas: small experiment idea: create a modified profile `int8_balanced_v1_noprefetch` with `kv_prefetch:false` and `calibration_mode: thorough` but run only against synthetic long-seq workload to see if fallbacks persist. If that fixes kernel coverage mismatch, we can try staged canary with long-seq gating.

Zara: also consider a fast runtime mitigation: add a per-request heuristic that monitors `kernel_fallback_count` and if it exceeds threshold X (e.g., 3) for the request, we immediately signal a transparent re-run on fp16 (best-effort) and return faster result; we'd need to be careful about double-charge and idempotency. This could be a very effective safety net for tail regressions.

Rishi: agree on safety net. For now prioritize rollback for customer and lab experiments. Tomas, can you add kernel coverage telemetry to the quant pipeline so future profiles include a coverage score? Also add a "predicted fallback risk" flag based on kernel coverage + calibration mode.

Tomas: on it. I'll add a job that compiles a coverage matrix by running typical op mix + seq_len grid and counting fallback occurrences. The job will emit coverage as a percentage and a risk score string. We'll also add it as a pre-rollout gate.

Maya: customer update: we forced fp16 for them and they reported immediate improvement. They still want to know what went wrong and whether int8 can be re-enabled safely. I told them we'll run a controlled test and get back within 24h.

Rishi: follow-ups assigned: - Tomas: kernel-coverage job + infra ticket to expand int8 kernels for missing ops - Zara: product work to add `force_fp16` customer toggle in console (fast mitigation) - QA: add long-seq + burst gating in rollout smoke tests - Support/Account: communicate ETA to customer (owner: Maya)

Maya: I'll draft a short incident summary for the account team and schedule the controlled canary with `noprefetch` and `thorough` calibration.

deploy-bot: rollout `quant-rollout/2026-03-15-01:18` -> paused by @Maya (reason: tail latency regression observed).

(90m) Rishi: monitoring shows p95/p99 for the customer's traffic back within baseline after the override. No more 502s. We'll keep the incident open until kernel coverage changes land.

Tomas: proposal for long-term: 1) add automatic calibration validation that runs a dictionary of worst-case op mixes and seq lengths and fails a profile if fallback risk > 10%; 2) add transparent-run-on-fp16 fallback with clear billing semantics; 3) improve docs for quant profile authors explaining `kv_prefetch` tradeoffs.

Zara: agreed. Also consider defaulting `calibration_mode` to `thorough` for public rollouts and exposing `fast` only for internal experiments.

Maya: closing notes: customer accepted current mitigation. I'll follow up with a scheduled canary with the revised profile and share results. Creating postmortem document in /incidents as requested. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

SupportBot: INC-2026-0315-19 moved to monitoring (pending infra follow-up).
